summary: The Q6 e-tron is Audi's first car on the 800-volt PPE platform it shares with the Porsche Macan Electric, sold here as a boxy SUV and a lower-roofed Sportback that Audi and the Australian outlets both file as an SUV. For MY27 Audi cut the range to four grades - the 75.8kWh rear-drive Q6 at $89,900 in either body and the SQ6 from $129,900 - dropping the long-range rear-drive performance and the dual-motor quattro grades, so the line-up is thinner than before with nothing between $89,900 and $129,900. Reviewers rate the cabin, screens and charging hardware a clear step above the cheaper MEB-based Q4, but mark the ride down as firm on the entry grade, which cannot be optioned with air suspension.
pros: The $89,900 entry Q6 and Q6 Sportback now list under the $91,661 fuel-efficient LCT threshold, so they avoid luxury car tax and qualify for the novated-lease FBT exemption on cars first held before 1 April 2027
800V architecture charges at 225kW on the Q6 and 270kW on the SQ6, roughly 10-80 per cent in about 21 minutes, against 175kW in the Audi Q4 e-tron
Braked towing of 2000kg on the rear-drive Q6 and 2400kg on the SQ6, above the Q4 e-tron 55 quattro's 1800kg and well clear of a Tesla Model Y's 1588kg
526L boot and 1517L with the 40:20:40 bench down in the SUV, plus a 64L frunk that swallows the charging cables
Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty, an eight-year/160,000km battery warranty and six years of roadside assistance
cons: MY27 deliveries start in the first half of 2027, and from 1 April 2027 the full FBT exemption is capped at $75,000, so a Q6 delivered after that date at $89,900 misses the full novated-lease exemption that the price cut was pitched at

The long-range performance and quattro grades are gone, so the 94.9kWh battery and all-wheel drive now come only in the SQ6 at $129,900, a $40,000 step from the entry car, and both SQ6 grades attract luxury car tax
Chasing Cars calls the entry rear-drive grade's ride 'very firm, tightly controlled and with next to no rebound' and notes air suspension cannot be ordered on it
Audi has not published MY27 range figures; the 462km WLTP figure for the entry SUV on 20-inch wheels is modest for the price next to the 485km Sportback
Choosing the Sportback body costs 15L of boot with the seats up and 144L with them down, and $5,000 extra on the SQ6
